# UD Laz BOUN

Language: [Laz](/lzz/index.html) (code: `lzz`)<br/>
Family: Kartvelian

This treebank has been part of Universal Dependencies since the UD v2.19 release.

The following people have contributed to making this treebank part of UD: Utku Türk, Kaan Bayar, Ayşegül Dilara Özercan, Görkem Yiğit Öztürk, Betül Bilgin.

Repository: [UD_Laz-BOUN](https://github.com/UniversalDependencies/UD_Laz-BOUN)<br />
Search this treebank on-line: [PML-TQ](https://lindat.mff.cuni.cz/services/pmltq/#!/treebank/udlzz_boun219)<br />
Download all treebanks: [UD 2.19](/#download)

License: CC BY-SA 4.0

Genre: grammar-examples

Questions, comments?
General annotation questions (either Laz-specific or cross-linguistic) can be raised in the [main UD issue tracker](https://github.com/UniversalDependencies/docs/issues).
You can report bugs in this treebank in the [treebank-specific issue tracker on Github](https://github.com/UniversalDependencies/UD_Laz-BOUN/issues).
If you want to collaborate, please contact [utkuturkboun&nbsp;(æt)&nbsp;gmail&nbsp;•&nbsp;com].
Development of the treebank happens outside the UD repository.
If there are bugs, either the original data source or the conversion procedure must be fixed.
Do not submit pull requests against the UD repository.

abstract = "This paper presents the first treebank for the Laz language, which is also the first Universal Dependencies Treebank for a South Caucasian language. We also aim to document an endangered language in a systematic fashion within an inherently cross-linguistic framework: the Universal Dependencies Project (UD). As of now, our treebank consists of 576 sentences and 2,306 tokens annotated in light with the UD guidelines. We evaluated the treebank on the dependency parsing task using a pretrained multilingual parsing model, and the results are comparable with other low-resourced treebanks with no training set. We aim to expand our treebank in the near future to include 1,500 sentences. The bigger goal for our project is to create a set of treebanks for minority languages in Anatolia."

<h2>Syntax</h2>

<h3>Auxiliary Verbs and Copula</h3>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 2 lemmas as copulas (<a>cop</a>). Examples: on, ortʼu.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 1 lemmas as auxiliaries (<a>aux</a>). Examples: on.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Relations Overview</h3>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 2 relation subtypes: <a>compound:redup</a>, <a>nmod:poss</a></li>
<li>The following 11 relation types are not used in this corpus at all: <a>expl</a>, <a>dislocated</a>, <a>discourse</a>, <a>appos</a>, <a>clf</a>, <a>fixed</a>, <a>list</a>, <a>orphan</a>, <a>goeswith</a>, <a>reparandum</a>, <a>dep</a></li>
</ul>
